results.fact: Gain vs loss on an out-and-back
results.evidence: Retry found no two agreeing car-to-car figures from the visitor center: one detailed guide gives 2,550 ft over 6.25 mi, the hike page gives 2,100 ft, and a trail-map listing gives 1,911 ft over 3.4 mi but from the Switchback Trailhead (a different start). No source states a car-to-car descent figure, so loss_ft cannot be changed and gain_ft has no second agreeing source. Would settle with a second independent visitor-center round-trip gain figure.

USGS point elevation at the pin's own coordinates reads about 5,157 ft, far below the stored 6,050 ft and consistent with a trail that tops out near 5,485 ft. No second source gives the overlook's elevation (the detailed guide mentions only an unnamed optional overlook, and 'Morse Creek Overlook' elsewhere is a roadside viewpoint on Hurricane Ridge Road), and the pin's placement itself is uncertain. Would settle with a second topo or trail-profile figure for this named overlook.

USGS point elevation at the trailhead pin reads 1,954 ft, and samples across the road-end parking lot read 1,958-1,965 ft. An independent GPS-track trail profile starting at the trailhead (47.9549, -123.8348) gives 592 m (1,942 ft). The park's own figure of 2,000 ft is the rounded version; a few hiking listings give lower values (1,825-1,877 ft) but nothing supports the stored 1,650 ft. The approach parenthetical also named the agency as its source, so it is rewritten plainly.

results.evidence: Retry searches again turned up only trips combining Arriva with Fisher Peak (11,200 ft over 18.5 mi) and a 25-mile round-trip listing with a 3,720-8,215 ft range; no page states an Arriva-only car-to-car gain, and the peak-list and trip-report pages that might (peakbagger, the hiking association's report) refused the fetch. Computing a figure is not allowed. Would settle with two Arriva-only trip logs stating total gain.

No source gives a one-way distance to Arriva's summit; available figures are round trips that include Fisher Peak (18.5 mi, 20 mi) or a 25-mile multi-peak loop, plus 3.5 mi to Easy Pass only. dist_km is left alone. Would settle with two Arriva-only trip logs giving the one-way or round-trip distance.

Sources genuinely differ by year and line: two guide services say ice up to 70 degrees, another guide's route profile says 60-85 degrees depending on line, and two separate trip reports (2017 and 2019) found a short vertical step at the crux. The row's own figures (max_angle 80, hazards 85, pitch grade 60-70 with a vertical note) each match one of these, so no single maximum is settled by agreeing sources. Would settle with an owner convention for the maximum (e.g. state the crux as a range that includes short near-vertical steps in some years).

results.fact: Which side of the ridge the snow approach climbs
results.correct_value: The standard start climbs snow on the ridge's west (Coleman Glacier) flank
results.evidence: A guide service's route profile states that from the Coleman Glacier flats on the west side of the lower North Ridge a 50-degree snow slope leads to the crest. A climbing database describes crossing the Coleman Glacier laterally to the base of the ridge and ascending snow slopes from there, with the Roosevelt Glacier (east side) only as an early-season alternate start. Both put the standard snow approach on the Coleman (west) side, matching the beta; the overview's 'left of the ridge crest' is an ambiguous relative direction, so it is restated by compass.
